questions.question: Define freedom of expression
questions.solution_html:
• Define freedom of expression
  • Freedom of expression is the fundamental human right to hold opinions without
  • interference and to seek, receive, and impart information and ideas through any media regardless of
  • frontiers. This right encompasses both verbal and non-verbal forms of communication, allowing
  • individuals to engage in public discourse and critique.

questions.question: Classify the types of news based on geographical location using relevant examples.
questions.solution_html:
• Classify the types of news based on geographical location using relevant examples.
  • News can be broadly classified by geographical scope into local, national, and international
  • news, each focusing on events within a specific boundary. Local news, such as a story about a new
  • town council ordinance, focuses on community affairs, while national news covers issues affecting an
  • entire country, like a presidential election. International news reports on significant events occurring
  • globally, such as treaty negotiations between multiple countries.

questions.question: Analyze the legal challenges presented by AI-generated media (audio, video, images) that realistically depict non-existent events. / [CO1, CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Analyze the legal challenges presented by AI-generated media (audio, video, images) that
  • realistically depict non-existent events.
  • General answer - AI-generated media depicting non-existent events presents significant legal
  • challenges, primarily concerning defamation, copyright, and the right of publicity. If this media falsely
  • portrays a person in a negative light, it can lead to defamation lawsuits and, if a likeness is used
  • without permission, may violate their right of publicity. Furthermore, the use of existing copyrighted
  • works to train AI models and generate new content raises complex issues regarding fair use and
  • intellectual property infringement.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Describe how you would prepare to cover an important political speech of a national leader
questions.solution_html:
• . Describe how you would prepare to cover an important political speech of a national
  • leader
  • To cover an important political speech, I would first conduct thorough research on the
  • leader's past statements, current policy positions, and the context surrounding the speech to
  • anticipate key themes. During the speech, I would actively listen for major announcements, shifts in
  • tone, or quotes that summarize the speech's main message, while also observing the audience's
  • reaction. Finally, I would immediately begin analyzing the speech's significance and its potential
  • political impact to frame my reporting accurately.
